Lessons.Title: Completing the Square (Part 2)
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: complete the square and solve monic quadratic equations with fractional coefficients, showing each rational step without rounding; analyze common errors in fraction arithmetic. Independently authored Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 7 Lesson 13 teacher https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/7/13/preparation.html and student https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/7/13/index.html (CC BY 4.0). The source emphasizes that the method is unchanged when rational values are awkward.

Original equation x²+(1/2)x=3/16. Half the x coefficient is1/4, whose square is1/16. Adding1/16 to both sides gives (x+1/4)²=4/16=1/4, so x+1/4=±1/2 and roots x=1/4 or−3/4. Check using sixteenths: for x1/4, x²1/16 plus(1/2)(1/4)=2/16 =>3/16; for x−3/4, x²9/16 plus−3/8=−6/16 =>3/16.

Second challenge x²+(3/2)x=1/4: half coefficient is3/4, square9/16; right becomes1/4+9/16=13/16; solutions x=(-3±√13)/4. The irrational exact forms are valid and should not be prematurely rounded. The method produces both roots even if a student expected only rational outputs.

Student task: explain the square-corner area with fractional parts, solve each equation, label both ± branches, identify a wrong common denominator in an incorrect peer solution and confirm exact roots. Teacher-scored rubric0–2 for fraction accuracy, equivalent transformations, full exact root set and coherent error analysis.

KeyConcepts.Title: Fractional completing term
KeyConcepts.Definition: For monic x²+bx, add (b/2)² even if b is a fraction.

KeyConcepts.Title: Equivalent fractions
KeyConcepts.Definition: Adding rational quantities requires common denominators.
KeyConcepts.Example: The completed square may have irrational roots.

KeyConcepts.Title: Exact radicals
KeyConcepts.Definition: Roots can be expressed with √ rather than rounded approximations.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Rounding irrational roots while claiming exact answers

SummaryPoints: Completing the square works with rational coefficients without changing its logic.
The first example has rational roots1/4 and−3/4.
The second has exact irrational roots(-3±√13)/4.
